cards.claim: Tiled Newton-Schulz reduces computational cost of orthogonalization compared to full-matrix Muon
cards.conditions: Dense parameter matrices in transformers where m ≤ n; square tiles of size t
cards.effect: Arithmetic cost decreases from O(kmn²) to O(kmt), where k is number of Newton-Schulz steps and t is tile size
cards.evidence: Mathematical analysis of tiled partition and independent tile computation
cards.quote: For square tiles, each tile requires arithmetic, and there are approximately tiles. Thus, up to lower-order padding effects, the leading Newton–Schulz work is (13) compared with the full-matrix cost.

cards.claim: SRAM-resident kernels for small tiles eliminate intermediate memory traffic overhead in Newton-Schulz iteration
cards.conditions: GPU implementation with tile size up to 64×64; SRAM budget sufficient for all Newton-Schulz iterations
cards.effect: Reduces intermediate HBM round trips between Newton-Schulz steps, making theoretical cost reduction visible in wall-clock time
cards.evidence: Implementation strategy for tile-size-dependent GPU kernel dispatch
cards.quote: HiMuon therefore uses an SRAM-resident kernel that keeps all Newton–Schulz iterations inside a single kernel, avoiding intermediate HBM round trips through the iteration loop.

cards.claim: Cross-layer batching of compatible tiles improves GPU utilization and reduces per-step overhead
cards.conditions: Multi-layer transformer models; tiles matching in shape, dtype, and kernel path; DDP or FSDP distributed training
cards.effect: Avoids GPU underutilization from launching small independent Newton-Schulz computations per matrix
cards.evidence: Implementation strategy addressing GPU execution efficiency
cards.quote: Launching one Newton–Schulz computation per matrix can underutilize the GPU because each launch may expose too little work. HiMuon thus groups compatible tiles across layers into larger batched Newton–Schulz calls.

cards.claim: Full-to-local tile-size schedule preserves early optimization quality while reducing cost in later phases
cards.conditions: Transformer pretraining with fixed schedule breakpoints (e.g., 1000 steps for DDP); shorter training runs
cards.effect: Maintains global spectral coupling during early optimization when gradient statistics are unsettled; switches to lower-cost tiled maps for remainder
cards.evidence: Empirical schedule design and optimization-phase motivation
cards.quote: The initial full-matrix phase preserves global spectral coupling during the earliest optimization steps, when gradient statistics and dominant directions are least settled. The optimizer then switches to lower-cost tiled maps for the remainder of training.

cards.claim: Tile size controls amount of retained spectral coupling, enabling trade-off between cost and interaction scope
cards.conditions: Any finite tile size below matrix dimensions
cards.effect: Larger tiles preserve more full-matrix spectral interaction; smaller tiles reduce cost and expose more independent parallel work
cards.evidence: Mathematical definition of tiled Newton-Schulz map and its distinction from full-matrix map
cards.quote: Larger tiles preserve more of the full-matrix interaction, while smaller tiles reduce the cost and expose more independent work.

cards.claim: Momentum buffers and weight decay remain unmodified under cross-layer batching
cards.conditions: Batched tile execution across layers; same optimizer state indexing
cards.effect: No change to optimizer dynamics, learning rate behavior, or interaction with momentum-based methods including lookahead
cards.evidence: Implementation design specification for optimizer state preservation
cards.quote: Momentum buffers, parameter tensors, and weight decay remain indexed by the original parameter, so cross-layer batching is an implementation strategy rather than a change to the optimizer update.

cards.claim: Under FSDP sharding, HiMuon requires no additional optimizer-internal communication
cards.conditions: Bank-sharded FSDP distributed training layout; rank owns complete matrices in local shard
cards.effect: Tiled Newton-Schulz computation is rank-local; eliminates communication overhead that would arise from optimizer modifications
cards.evidence: Distributed training implementation and FSDP layout analysis
cards.quote: Under the bank-sharded Fully Sharded Data Parallel (FSDP) layout used in our experiments, same-shape matrices are stored along a leading batch axis, so each rank owns a subset of complete matrices in its local shard. The tiled Newton–Schulz computation is therefore rank-local and does not require an optimizer-internal all-gather.

cards.claim: Tile size is a runtime-configurable parameter that does not require optimizer state reset
cards.conditions: Finite tile sizes applied during training; optimizer state cached across reconfigurations
cards.effect: Enables dynamic tile-size schedules (e.g., full-to-local) without loss of momentum or other optimizer buffers
cards.evidence: Algorithm design specification and GPU implementation reconfiguration mechanism
cards.quote: The tile size is exposed as a runtime parameter rather than being fixed at optimizer construction. A reconfigure() routine updates the tile-dependent execution plan when changes. ... The optimizer state itself, including the momentum buffers, is independent of the tile size and is preserved across reconfiguration.
